غَاذٌّ [act. part. n. of 1, q. v.: as such signifying A vein incessantly bleeding. (L.) ―
-b2- Also A recrudescence (عَرَب [inf. n. of عَرِبَ], so in the O, in copies of the K غَرَب, and in the CK غَرْب, [app. a mistranscription suggested by another explanation of غَاذٌّ which will be found in what follows,]) in any part of the body. (L, K.) AZ says, what we call العَرَبُ, the Arabs term الغَاذُّ. (O.) One says of a camel that has had a gall on the back which has healed but is, or becomes, moist [or exuding], بِهِ غَاذٌّ [He has a gall which has healed but is moist, or constantly discharging, or exuding]. (S, O, L.) ―
-b3- And A vein, or duct, in the eye, [also called غَرْبٌ,] which flows incessantly. (L, K.) In this sense, and in that immediately preceding, it is a subst. like كَاهِلٌ and غَارِبٌ. (L.) ＝
-A2- And الغَاذُّ signifies الحِسُّ: one says, قَطَعَ ٱللّٰهُ غَاذَّ فُلَانٍ i. e. حِسَّهُ [app. meaning May God cause to cease the sound of such a one]. (Ibn-'Abbád, O)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
